newsitem.title: USA: K-tel to sell some music assets for $35 million.
newsitem.headline: K-tel to sell some music assets for $35 million.

text.p: K-tel International Inc., known for its once ubiquitous televisions commercials hawking pop music collections, said Monday it will sell most of its music business to Platinum Entertainment Inc. for $35 million.

K-tel has a catalogue of more than 3,500 owned or controlled recordings, including performances by Chubby Checker, Bobby Sherman, Leslie Gore, Percy Sledge, Lee Greenwood and hundreds of others. K-tel also packages and markets of pre-recorded music.
Platinum said it will continue to use K-tel's distribution system to sell the music collections through retailers like Kmart Corp. and Best Buy Co. Inc.

Under the terms of the agreement, Downers Grove, Ill.-based Platinum will acquire K-tel's worldwide music business assets, except for K-tel's European music business, through the purchase of the stock of K-tel International (USA) Inc. and Dominion Entertainment Inc., both wholly-owned subsidiaries of K-tel International, the companies said.
Plymouth, Minn.-based K-tel will retain its music business in Eastern and Western Europe and the former Soviet Republic.

K-tel also will receive an exclusive license to use the Dominion and K-tel (USA) music catalogue in these territories and a non-exclusive license of the catalogue in Africa and the Middle East, the companies said. The licenses will be royalty free except for third party amounts payable from the use of the masters.
"This transaction allows our shareholders to better realise the intrinsic value of K-tel's catalogue of master recordings," K-tel President David Weiner said.
"This valuable asset is carried on our balance sheet at only nominal value and, in our opinion, has not been adequately reflected in our company's public market capitalisation."

K-tel will continue to focus on North American operations in music commercials, video, consumer products and direct response businesses, the company said. The businesses it keeps accounted for $43.6 million in gross revenues for its fiscal year ended June 30, 1996, while the business it is selling accounted for $42.6 million, the company said.
